# dsh-publisher-radar · Publisher Radar

**A market-gap radar for DSH plugin developers — see which directions are still open before
you writ

p radar for DSH plugin developers — see which directions are still open before
you write the code.**

It answers one question: **which corners of this market are empty?** Several thousand
plugins are sp

lit by category and then by topic, and every topic is tagged empty / thin /
contested / crowded, so

"what should I build next" becomes something you can look at rather
than guess. Browsing the full ma

rket and copying install commands is what falls out of the
same catalog, not the point.
简体中文 · MIT · Publishing
## Why

The DSH marketplace passed **6,000 plugins** in 2026 and keeps growing — the panel always
shows the
current count, because it reads the catalog rather than a number written here.

The bigger that market gets, the harder "what should I build" becomes. What blocks a plugin
author i

s rarely writing the code; it is finishing it and finding out somebody already shipped
the same thin
g. Today that judgement comes from scrolling the list and going on memory:

1. *Is this direction already taken?* — names collide (five authors ship a
`dsh-plugin-doctor`), whi

le the real competitor describes itself in completely different
words and never shows up in a name s

earch.
2. *Is there still a gap inside a busy category?* — big categories like `ui` or `dev` hide
do
zens of topics, some with thirty plugins and some with one or two.
Publisher Radar splits the catalog by topic and makes "what's empty" visible at a glance.
## What you see

A sidebar entry and five model tools — all from one catalog. **The topic view is the core**;
the res
t is supporting cast.
| Surface | What it does |
| `radar_gaps` | **The one you'll use most**: which topics have 0–3 plugins, ranked so the emptiest

directions come first |
| Panel「方向 · Topics」 | The same view with a UI: category → topic → plugins,

four coverage levels, both sort directions |
| `radar_plugin` | Who already took this topic, name or

author — dedupe and competitor lookup |
| `radar_market` | How big is the market, what leads, how e

ach category is distributed |
| `radar_mine` | My downloads, stars, catalog presence, category rank

|
| `radar_checkup` | Will this folder survive a market install? |
| **Publisher Radar** (sidebar) |
Browse the whole market: search, category filter, paging, sort by downloads / stars / date; open on

e for its install command |
| Panel「设置 · Settings」 | Track your own npm packages; optional GitHub to
ken (never required) |
## Zero configuration, on purpose
Nothing below is required to use it, and there is no setup step:

- **Catalog** — raced across the canonical host, unpkg, jsDelivr, and the npm China
mirror (`dsh-plu

gin-catalog` tarball). Whichever answers first wins; results are
cached six hours. Measured from a m

ainland network: 6.7 s when the canonical host is
blocked, 0.7 s through the mirror, 50 ms from cach

e.
- **Stars** — live from GitHub when the package has a repository (the catalog's URL, or
the one n

pm publishes); otherwise the catalog's snapshot. A failure falls back
silently instead of showing a

broken number.
- **Your plugins** — read from the panel's Settings field (「设置」in the UI), or
auto-de

tected when the workspace is your plugin folder (a `package.json` with
`dsh.bundle`). A local `file:

` package that was never published still resolves — its
manifest is in the profile.

## Honest caveats

- Coverage is a **lexical** match over `name + description`, so it over-counts
(`ats` hits `formats`

cs do **not** cover every plugin (about half match none). Browsing is the
full catalog; the topic ra

nking is for deciding what to build. Do not mix the two.
- `checkup` judges packaging and supply-cha
in shape, not code quality or security.
## Privacy

- Public data only, nothing uploaded.
- **Writing: two files.** The catalog cache (`catalog.json`, 8

.7 MB, six-hour TTL) and
the settings you save in the panel (`config.json`). No history, no session

data, no
copies of anything of yours.
- A GitHub token, if you provide one, is stored in that `confi

g.json` in plain text on
this machine and is never returned by the API — only "a token is set".
- `r

adar_checkup` reads the folder you point it at and writes nowhere.
- The panel's data is served by y
our local DSH web server, same-origin, `no-store`.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`test:install` is the one that matters before a release: it takes the tarball a user
would download,

`npm install`s it into an empty directory, then imports the installed
copy and asserts it registers

its five tools and two routes. Packaging mistakes that
pass a source-tree test (a missing file, an
absolute `name:` in the patch) fail here.

No build step, no runtime dependencies. `lib/` ships as authored; the browser half is
hand-written p
lain JS (no JSX, no bundler), the same shape DSH's own panels use.
## Limitations

- The catalog is a curated list, not npm itself; an unlisted plugin is invisible here.
- `added` dat
es come from the catalog, so a very fresh plugin may not be dated yet.
